evidence: Compared word by word with SOURCE.txt. Draft: 'So each can correct the other.' Words it replaces: 'So these modes can correct each other.' His published line: 'Let the modes correct each other.' The draft is exactly the sentence the_change names (Emulate's, no fix by the writer). Against the replaced words, 'these modes' becomes 'each' and 'each other' becomes 'the other'; 'So' and 'can correct' are kept. Preservation: the claim is the same, that the things the four 'Without ...' lines set side by side (love and analysis, intuitive signals and testing) can correct one another; nothing is added (no claim, condition, person, number or named entity) and who does what is unchanged (each corrects and is corrected). Two small shifts, neither of which I count as a change of meaning. (1) The word 'modes' is gone, and it appears nowhere else in this section, so his word for these things no longer shows; the referent is still plain from the four lines just before. (2) 'each ... the other' is a two-party form where 'these modes ... each other' was general; the four lines before it make two pairs, so it reads as 'in each pair, each corrects the other', which is exactly what those lines show, not a narrowing to the last pair. Both the replaced words and the draft already turn his 'Let ... correct' (an instruction) into 'can correct' (a possibility); this change leaves that as it was. The change claims to put nothing back, so nothing promised is missing (the ledger's T14 and T15 lines saying it 'puts back the author's own point that Emulate dropped' do not describe this change, which is Emulate's sentence unaltered). Reads right in context: 6 words, no typos, it follows 'Without intuitive signals the testing can be dead.' smoothly and leads into 'It's got to lead somewhere!'. Tells: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal draft in its context. PRESENT: T29 (a 'So ...' conclusion: the four 'Without' lines already make the point and this line states it as their consequence; I disagree with the writer's ABSENT) and T20 (a short landing; the neighbouring paragraphs also end on short lines, 'Nobody needs to win!', 'It can be peaceful but also precise.', 'It's got to lead somewhere!', so this section has a run of them). Both justified: the sentence is the only place the paragraph states his point ('Let the modes correct each other'), which can't be cut or merged without losing it; it is a plain statement, not an antithesis, triad or quotable line; it replaces a 'So ... can correct' closer with the same kind in the same place and job, so the change adds no new instance and no neater one; and the 'So' ties it to the lines before it. Judged absent: T17 (a consequence tied to the four lines, not a free-standing principle), T12 (the A/B pairs before it are the argument for mutual correction, not packaging), C02 (see (2)). Linter: 'B7 short landing at paragraph end' accepted for the reasons just given (his thesis line, like-for-like with the sentence it replaces, plain not polished). 'D9 follows the source order' accepted: one sentence replacing one sentence in the same place, and T13 and T09 have nothing to flag in it.
